title: Eder Militão Confirmed Out of 2026 World Cup — Real Madrid Defender Undergoes Surgery for Hamstring Injury
detail: Real Madrid and the Brazilian Football Confederation confirmed that defender Eder Militão will miss the 2026 World Cup after undergoing surgery for a ruptured proximal tendon of the biceps femoris (hamstring) in his left leg — an injury requiring approximately five months of recovery. The surgery was performed in early May, ruling him out well past the tournament's July 19 final. Brazil's defensive options are already stretched: the squad has lost both Rodrygo (ACL/meniscus, confirmed out in March) and Estevao (Grade-4 hamstring, listed as doubtful). With Militão out, Brazil coach Dorival Júnior is expected to rely on the Marquinhos–Gabriel Magalhaes center-back pairing as the first-choice defensive partnership, with Bremer likely on the bench. Militão's Real Madrid partner Antonio Rüdiger remains available for Germany. Brazil open Group C on June 13 at Dallas against Japan, with Serbia (June 18) and Australia (June 22) completing their group-stage schedule — all at AT&T Stadium.

media.caption: Eder Militão ruled out of 2026 World Cup after surgery for hamstring rupture — Brazil loses a third key player to injury ahead of June 13 opener vs Japan

title: Analysis: FIFA Congress in Vancouver Exposed Deep Political Rifts — Iran Absence, Palestine-Israel Confrontation, and Diplomacy Failures
detail: Analysis published on May 2 assessed the political rifts exposed by the 76th FIFA Congress in Vancouver — characterized as one of the most diplomatically charged FIFA Congresses in recent history. Three major flashpoints: (1) Iran's absence — the Iranian football federation's entire delegation was denied entry to Canada at Toronto Pearson Airport, making Iran the only of 211 FIFA member associations absent from the roll call, an unprecedented occurrence so close to a tournament; (2) the Palestine-Israel confrontation — PFA president Rajoub's refusal to shake hands on stage with his Israeli counterpart, and the last-minute withdrawal of the suspension motion under member association pressure; and (3) FIFA's structural limitations — Infantino confirmed Iran's participation against the will of the Iranian government, exposing the fault line between FIFA's governance framework (which recognizes football federations, not governments) and the political reality on the ground. Analysts observed that Infantino's Iran confirmation — without any diplomatic resolution of the underlying security question — pushed the crisis into the squad submission phase (June 1 deadline) without resolution. The Congress also notably failed to produce any formal FIFA commitment on immigration enforcement near venues or fan safety for at-risk communities.

media.caption: Post-Congress analysis: The Vancouver FIFA Congress exposed unresolved political fractures — Iran's absence, Palestine-Israel confrontation, and FIFA's inability to resolve security questions before the June 1 squad deadline
